steps.name: Count matrix QC and sample-level quality check
steps.context: Dataset: human liver bulk RNA-seq, 12,000 genes x 6 samples (3 drug-treated vs 3 control), raw gene-level counts exported from Salmon; the data profile does not record whether Salmon length correction was applied. Single batch, unpaired design.
steps.question: Are the 6 liver samples (3 treated, 3 control) technically sound and comparable, and which genes carry enough count data to support a 3-vs-3 differential test?
steps.description: Load /eval-four-models-v2-without-two-group-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 6 samples) and metadata.csv (6 x 2), verify sample-name alignment, library-size distribution and count integrity (integers, no negatives), filter genes with negligible counts (e.g. count >= 10 in at least 3 samples), then compute variance-stabilized/logCPM PCA, sample-to-sample distances and treatment-vs-control separation to detect outlier samples before any DE testing. Inspect whether the count column values are integral: raw Salmon gene counts are integers, whereas length-corrected countsFromAbundance output is not — record which case this is, since it determines whether standard DESeq2 size factors apply or the matrix must be handled as length-scaled counts.
acceptance_criteria: counts.csv parsed: 12,000 genes x 6 samples confirmed against metadata.csv sample IDs
QC report with library sizes, pre/post-filter gene counts, and PCA sample clustering saved to T1S1 outputs
Explicit statement whether any sample is a candidate outlier, with the numeric evidence behind it

steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control (DESeq2)
steps.context: Design: ~condition, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, human liver. Input is the QC-filtered gene-level count matrix from T1S1. DESeq2 1.52 and apeglm 1.34 are installed in the R track.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between drug-treated and control liver samples, and what are their effect sizes under the 3-vs-3 design?
steps.description: Run DESeq2 (R, DESeq2 1.52) on the filtered matrix with design ~condition (treated vs control), Wald test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Apply apeglm LFC shrinkage for ranking and interpretation — essential at n=3/group where raw LFCs on low-count genes are wildly variable. Produce the full results table, MA plot, dispersion-fit plot and volcano plot. Report DE-gene counts at FDR < 0.05, < 0.10 and < 0.20, because at this sample size the 0.05 threshold alone will understate both the signal and the uncertainty. State in the output that dispersion is estimated from only 4 residual degrees of freedom, so per-gene SEs are wide and padj values are correspondingly unstable.
acceptance_criteria: Full DESeq2 results table (gene, baseMean, log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) written as CSV covering all tested genes
Shrunken LFC table produced; reported DE-gene counts at FDR < 0.05, < 0.10 and < 0.20 with the FDR-threshold sensitivity stated explicitly
MA plot, dispersion-fit plot and volcano plot saved; dispersion fit inspected for convergence given only 6 samples
Results table row count equals filtered gene count from T1S1 (or documented discrepancy)

steps.name: Replicate-confidence audit: LOO stability and permutation null
steps.context: Observed DE results and the QC-stable sample set come from T1S1/T1S2. The design has 6 samples; leave-one-out leaves 2 treated vs 3 control or 3 vs 2, which DESeq2 still fits but with reduced power — LOO results must be reported as stability diagnostics, not as corrected p-values.
steps.question: How confident can we be in the DE calls — and in the set of DE genes — given only 3 replicates per group?
steps.description: Quantify the stability of the T1S2 calls under resampling, since 3-vs-3 is the smallest design where DESeq2 dispersion estimation functions at all. Three diagnostics: (1) leave-one-out reruns — refit DESeq2 six times dropping each sample in turn, and measure Jaccard overlap of the FDR<0.05 gene sets, sign concordance of shrunken LFCs, and rank stability (Kendall tau on signed statistics) against the full model; (2) permutation calibration — for each of the 20 possible 3/3 label assignments (including the true one), rerun the same DESeq2 pipeline and record how many genes reach FDR<0.05, yielding an empirical null distribution for the DE-gene count and an empirical calibration of how unusual the observed count is; (3) effect-size sanity — report the width of shrunken-LFC confidence intervals for the top hits so the reader sees the precision actually supported. Conclude with a plain-language verdict: which calls are robust to the loss of any single replicate, and which rest on a single sample's signal.
acceptance_criteria: Table of 6 leave-one-out reruns: DE-gene counts at FDR<0.05, overlap (Jaccard) with the full-model set, and LFC sign-concordance rates
Rank-stability metric (e.g. Kendall tau of signed statistics across LOO runs) for top-ranked genes
Exact permutation calibration over all 20 label assignments: observed DE count vs the null distribution, with an empirical calibration statement
Final confidence verdict combining internal (LOO/permutation) evidence, explicitly warning against extending it to external cohorts

steps.name: Pathway-level interpretation of the DE signal
steps.context: The organism is human, so the WikiPathways Homo sapiens GMT (HGNC symbols) under /mnt/refs is the correct resource — not the rat or mouse files also staged. Input is the full ranked gene list from T1S2; fgsea 1.38 is installed.
steps.question: Do the treated-vs-control DE results converge on coherent biological pathways despite the small replicate number?
steps.description: Convert DE results to a ranked list (signed Wald statistic or shrunken LFC x -log10(p) rank metric over all filtered genes) and run FGSEA against the WikiPathways human pathway set (HGNC-symbol GMT provisioned under /mnt/refs). Map gene identifiers to HGNC symbols if the count matrix uses Ensembl or Entrez IDs, using the staged human UniProt ID-mapping table if needed, and report the mapping rate. If the FDR<0.05 DE list from T1S2 is non-empty, additionally run a conservative over-representation check on it; with a small DE list the ranked-list FGSEA is the primary analysis and ORA the secondary. Interpret pathway hits as hypothesis-level context only, given n=3/group.
acceptance_criteria: FGSEA results table (pathway, size, ES, NES, pval, padj) written as CSV; if no pathway reaches FDR<0.25 this is reported as a finding, not suppressed
Minimum pathway size and max size documented; number of DE genes mapping to pathway symbols reported
If the human pathway resource or ID mapping is unavailable, the step logs its absence and terminates gracefully without blocking the run

plan.title: Liver 3v3 drug-treatment DE with confidence audit
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a minimal but valid bulk RNA-seq design: 12,000 gene-level counts from Salmon across 6 human liver samples, 3 drug-treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. The research question has two parts — which genes differ, and how much to trust the answer at n=3 per group — so the plan pairs a standard DE workflow with an explicit replicate-confidence audit rather than stopping at a DE table. Step order: (1) QC and low-count filtering to establish a stable gene universe and check for outlier samples, since one bad sample out of six distorts a 3-vs-3 contrast more than any statistical fix can repair; (2) DESeq2 differential expression with apeglm shrinkage, because at 4 residual degrees of freedom raw LFCs and SEs are unstable and shrinkage plus multi-threshold reporting is the honest way to present effect sizes; (3) a confidence audit quantifying stability directly — leave-one-out refits, an exact permutation null over all 20 possible 3/3 label assignments, and CI widths for top hits — which answers the 'how confident can we be' half of the question with numbers rather than hedging; (4) FGSEA against the human WikiPathways GMT on the full ranked list, chosen over over-representation because a ranked-list test extracts pathway signal even when the FDR<0.05 list is thin at this sample size. All steps run on the staged 12000x7 counts.csv and 6x2 metadata.csv; the human-only reference files are used because the organism is Homo sapiens.
